motions.title: Call-in of Executive Decision - Purchase of Synergy Education Management System
motions.full_text: That the Board considers the requisition of the Key Executive Decision and determines whether to uphold it.
motions.opposition_strategy: The opposition will focus on the 100,000 pound typographical error as evidence of financial incompetence. They will argue that the decision maker lacked authority because the total contract value exceeds 1 million pounds when VAT is included. They will also challenge the direct award to Access UK Limited, claiming a lack of evidence for value for money and questioning if other suppliers like CACI or LiquidLogic were properly considered.
motions.ruling_group_response: State clearly that the 100,000 pound discrepancy was a typographical error in the report text only and did not affect the actual pricing schedule or contract. Clarify that for constitutional delegation, figures are net of VAT because VAT is reclaimable by the Council. Emphasise that a direct award via the YPO framework is a legally compliant route that avoids massive migration costs, staff retraining, and operational risks to statutory education services.

amendment_predictions.amendment_angle: To refer the decision back to Cabinet with a requirement for a full external audit of the procurement process.
amendment_predictions.counter: Argue that this would cause unnecessary delay to a statutory service system. The Monitoring Officer has already verified the corrected report and the legal framework used.

key_data_points: Total contract value is 1,033,325.26 pounds including VAT
Typo corrected from 256,101.66 pounds to 356,101.66 pounds for the extension period
Direct award via YPO Software Application Solutions Framework 1095 Lot 11

motions.title: Endorsement of the Draft Scrutiny Protocol
motions.full_text: That the Overview and Scrutiny Board endorses the draft Scrutiny Working Protocol, recommends that the People and Place Overview and Scrutiny Sub-Committees and Cabinet also endorse it, and apply its principles and expectations in future scrutiny and executive work.
motions.opposition_strategy: Opposition members may argue that the protocol is an attempt to 'manage' or 'muzzle' them by formalising conduct. They may complain about the timeliness of information sharing from Cabinet members.
motions.ruling_group_response: Frame the protocol as a tool that empowers scrutiny by establishing clear expectations for Cabinet to share information early. Highlight that it respects the separate roles of the Executive and Scrutiny while promoting a 'critical friend' approach that improves outcomes for residents.

amendment_predictions.amendment_angle: Adding stricter timelines for Cabinet responses to scrutiny recommendations.
amendment_predictions.counter: Accept as a 'friendly amendment' if the timelines are reasonable, as it demonstrates a commitment to transparency.

key_data_points: Protocol supports recommendations from the 2025/26 annual review
Constitution takes precedence in any case of inconsistency

questions.question_text: Can the Council confirm the precise legal entity receiving the contract and whether they are correctly appointed under the YPO framework?
recommended_answer_points: The legal contracting entity is Access UK Limited
The Access Group is merely a trading name used in some documentation for recognition
Access UK Limited is the formally appointed supplier on YPO Framework 001095
questions.trap_explanation: The opposition is looking for any technicality to invalidate the procurement process. Any ambiguity in the supplier name could be used to claim a breach of procurement rules.

questions.question_text: Why was the decision made by a Director if the value exceeds the 1 million pound threshold for Cabinet Member approval?
recommended_answer_points: The Financial Scheme of Delegation uses figures net of VAT
The net value is 861,104.38 pounds, which falls within the Strategic Director's authority
Regardless, Cllr Kevin Gill as Cabinet Member has now been identified as the decision maker to ensure maximum transparency
questions.trap_explanation: This targets a perceived conflict between the Contract Procedure Rules (which include VAT) and the Financial Scheme of Delegation (which excludes VAT).

tactical_scenarios.scenario: Opposition moves to uphold the call-in and refer the Synergy decision back to Cabinet based on the financial typo.
tactical_scenarios.counter: The Cabinet Member (Cllr Gill) should intervene early to acknowledge the typo, confirm it is corrected, and explain that the underlying data is sound. Focus on the risk to school admissions and SEND finance if the system is not renewed.
tactical_scenarios.standing_order: Paragraph 17 of Overview and Scrutiny Committee Rules

tactical_scenarios.scenario: A recorded vote is demanded on the Synergy call-in to create a public record of the 'financial error'.
tactical_scenarios.counter: Ensure all ruling group members are present and briefed. Do not shy away from the vote. Frame the vote as being for or against the continuity of essential education services.

time_management.recommended_time_saving: Move quickly through the Minutes and Announcements to allow maximum time for the Synergy call-in debate.

speakers.name: Cllr Kevin Gill
key_points: The system is vital for statutory duties like school admissions and SEND
The typo was administrative and has been corrected
The procurement is legally sound via the YPO framework

speakers.name: Tara Geere
key_points: Risks of migrating to a new provider
